definition.val: A narrowing of the biparietal diameter (i.e., of the transverse distance between the protuberances of the two parietal bones of the skull).
A forehead with abnormal flatness.

An abnormality of the cheek- one of two bilateral soft tissue facial structures in the region of the face inferior to the eyes and between the nose and the ear. "Buccal" means relating to the cheek. The cheek is part of the midface

This is a description previously used to describe a facial form characterized by a short, upturned nose, wide mouth, widely spaced eyes, and full cheeks. Because of the imprecision in this definition it is preferable to describe these features precisely. This term is retained because it was often used in the past, but it should not be used for new annotations.
Increased susceptibility to viral infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral infection.
A combined immunodeficiency primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.
An immunodeficiency defined by the absent or suboptimal functioning of one of the complement system proteins.
Absence or extremely low level of IgA, IgM, and IgM in the circulation.

Deficiency of secretory IgA (polymers of 2-4 IgA monomers are linked by two additional chains) and is the primary antibody response at the mucosal level, where it forms immune complexes with pathogens and allergens.
A reduced level of the complement component C8 in circulation.

comments: The eighth component of complement (C8) plays an important role in the function of membrane attack complex (MAC) that is generated on target cells upon activation of the complement system. MAC is generated by sequential addition of C5b, C6, C7, C8, and C9 molecules, which results in the transmembrane pore and eventual cell lysis. Individuals with C8 deficiency tend to have recurrent neisserial infections.

definition.val: Excessive growth of the bones of cranium, i.e., of the skull.
Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the frontal bone.

synonyms.val: Enlargement of the inner surface of the frontal bone
Hypertrophy of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Increased ossification of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Overgrowth of the inside of the frontal bone
Thick inner surface of the frontal bone
Thick internal surface of the frontal bone
Excessive growth of inner surface of the frontal bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Overgrowth of the inner surface of the frontal bone

definition.val: A characteristic appearance resulting from defective ossification of craniofacial bones.

comments: Note: This term is used in the medical literature to describe an appearance of the face of patients with Crouzon syndrome (also called craniofacial dysostosis), which is characterized by acrocephaly, exophthalmos, hypertelorism, strabismus, parrot-beaked nose, and hypoplastic maxilla. This is thus probably mainly used as a bundled term and should be replaced by better descriptions in the future.

definition.val: Premature closure of the coronal suture of skull.
A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the sagittal suture.

synonyms.val: Early closure of midline skull joint

definition.val: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the lambdoidal suture.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.

comments: Erythrocytes are normally biconcave rather than spherical.

definition.val: The presence of elliptical, cigar-shaped erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear.

comments: Elliptocytes (ovalocytes) are abnormal erythrocytes ranging from slightly oval to elongated cigar-shaped forms.

definition.val: The presence of erythrocytes with a mouth-shaped (stoma) area of central pallor on peripheral blood smear.
The presence of abnormally shaped erythrocytes.

comments: General description for abnormally shaped erythrocytes.

definition.val: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as fulminant if there is onset of encephalopathy within 4 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.
A groove of the skin immediately in front of the ear.

synonyms.val: Skin groove in front of the ear
Skin sulcus in front of the ear

definition.val: A rudimentary tag of ear tissue often containing a core of cartilage and located just in back of the auricle (outer part of the ear).

nodes.lbl: Abnormality of the middle ear ossicles

definition.val: An abnormality of the middle-ear ossicles (three small bones called malleus, incus, and stapes) that are contained within the middle ear and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth (cochlea).
A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal.
The presence of a dilated inner part of external acoustic meatus.

nodes.lbl: Exostosis of the external auditory canal

definition.val: A benign bony growth projecting outward from a bone surface within the external auditory canal.
Pits in the earlobes at the location where ears are typically pierced for earrings.
Lack of measurable response to stimulation of auditory evoked potentials.
Benign congenital lesion of the postauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.
Small indentation anterior to the insertion of the ear.

comments: Preauricular cysts and sinuses are ectodermal remnants from an aberrant development of the auditory tubercles, tend to be bilateral and are localized anterior to the tragus of the ear. The preauricular sinus is a benign congenital lesion of the preauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit. It is also known as preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst. It can be asymptomatic or present as an infected and discharging sinus. It presents as a small pit adjacent to the external ear usually located at the anterior margin of the ascending limb of the helix. The preauricular sinus is variably also termed a preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst.

synonyms.val: Pit in front of the ear

definition.val: An abnormality of the C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage, normally 16 to 20 in number, that occupy the anterior two-thirds of the circumference of the trachea (the posterior portion of the ring is completed by fibrous and smooth muscle tissue).
Chronic inflammation of the bronchi.
A congenital defect in the occipital region of the skull, covered by skin of the scalp and containing meninges or remnants of glial or neural tissues.

nodes.lbl: Aplasia cutis congenita over the scalp vertex

definition.val: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp vertex, often just lateral to the midline.
Hyperostosis (bony overgrowth) of the mandible.

comments: This bundled term will be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO.

definition.val: The anterior fontanelle generally ossifies by around the 18th month of life. A persistent open anterior fontanelle is diagnosed if closure is delayed beyond this age.

nodes.lbl: Aplasia cutis congenita over parietal area

definition.val: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp in the parietal area.

synonyms.val: Absent cutis congenita over parietal area

definition.val: The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.

A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.
Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.
Stagnation of head growth seen as flattening of the head circumference curve.

An abnormality of head shape characterized by the presence of a short, wide head as well as a pointy or conical form of the top of the head owing to premature closure of the coronal and lambdoid sutures.
The presence of an abnormally large skull with onset at birth.

synonyms.val: Head circumference large for gestational age

definition.val: Excessive growth of the calvaria.

comments: The calvaria (skull cap) is made up of the frontal, occipital, right and left parietal, right and left temporal, sphenoid, and ethmoid bones, and thus comprises the upper dome-like part of the skull and does not include the lower jaw.

definition.val: An enlargement of the posterior fontanelle relative to age-dependent norms.
An abnormally increased width of the cranial fontanelles and sutures.

comments: This term indicates that both the fontanelles and the sutures are widely patent and thus represents a severe form of delay in closure of the fontanelles/sutures.

definition.val: Excessive growth of the craniofacial bones.

synonyms.val: Excessive bone growth of the skull and face

comments: This bundled term will be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO and should not be used for new annotations.

definition.val: Absence or abnormal closure of the posterior portion of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture).

nodes.lbl: Chronic rhinitis due to narrow nasal airway

synonyms.val: Chronic nasal inflammation due to narrow nasal airway

definition.val: Bilateral absence (atresia) of the posterior nasal aperture (choana).

synonyms.val: Bilateral blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
Bilateral obstruction of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

definition.val: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells.

comments: The islets of Langerhans contain the alpha cells (producing glucagon), beta cells (insulin and amylin), delta cells (somatostatin),PP cells (pancreatic polypeptide), and the epsilon cells (ghrelin).

definition.val: Increased length of the hairs of the eyebrows.
Reduced or lacking hair growth in the temporal region (i.e., around the temples on the side of the skull).

synonyms.val: Reduced hair growth in temporal region

nodes.lbl: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft

synonyms.val: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft

definition.val: Reduced or lacking hair growth in a generalized distribution.
Excessive, increased hair growth located in the sacral region.
Anterior cervical hypertrichosis (ACH) or 'hairy throat' refers to the presence of a tuft of terminal hair on the anterior neck, just above the laryngeal prominence.
A confluent, generalized overgrowth of silvery blonde to gray lanugo hair at birth.

comments: Hypertrichosis refers to excessive, abnormal hairiness.

synonyms.val: Hair loss on scalp from scarring condition

definition.val: Generalized excessive, abnormal hairiness.
A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the cervical spine.
Increased bone density affecting the bones of the spine (vertebral column).
Bulbous appearance of the anterior vertebral bodies, such that the vertebral bodies have the greatest vertical height anteriorly as well as bulbous anterior superior-inferior contours.
Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the vertebral bodies.
Increased top to bottom height of vertebral bodies.
An abnormality of the shape of the thoracic vertebra T11 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).

synonyms.val: Anterior wedging of the 11th thoracic vertebra

definition.val: Sclerosis (increased density) affecting vertebral end plates.
An excessive concavity of the anterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.

comments: One cause of anterior scalloping is an aortic aneurysm, which because of its pulsatile pressure can cause a convex defect along the anterior surface of an adjacent vertebra body. The defect may have a sclerotic margin.

definition.val: Exaggerated concavity of the anterior or posterior surface of the vertebral body, i.e., the upper and lower vertebral endplates are hollowed inward.

comments: This finding has been called fish or codfish vertebra because of the characteristic biconcave form of fish vertebral bodies.

definition.val: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance beween the vertebral endplates affecting the thoracic spine.

nodes.lbl: Hump-shaped mound of bone in central and posterior portions of vertebral endplate

definition.val: Three ossification sites are present in typical vertebral bodies (C3-L5): a single ossification center in the vertebral body, and one each in the two neural arches. This term applies if there are additional vertebral ossification centers present during the development and maturation of the spine.

nodes.lbl: Absent or minimally ossified vertebral bodies

definition.val: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of the vertebra L5 with intact overlying skin.

Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C2 and C3, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development, leading to a short neck with a low hairline at the back of the head, and restricted mobility of the upper spine.
A lack of bone mineralization of the vertebral bodies.
A lack of ossification of the vertebral bodies.

nodes.lbl: Anterior beaking of lower thoracic vertebrae

definition.val: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the lower thoracic vertebral bodies.
Anterior mislocalization of the dens of the axis.
An abnormal narrowing of the lumbar spinal canal.

comments: Symptoms of lumbar spinal canal stenosis include pseudoclaudication (pain, numbness,, or weakness induced by walking and relieved by rest; the prefix pseudo is used to differentiate this manifestation from claudication, which has similar symptoms but is caused by peripheral artery disease).

definition.val: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of S1 with intact overlying skin.
A discontinuity of the vertebral arch, i.e., of the posterior part of a vertebra.
Butterfly vertebrae have a cleft through the body of the vertebrae and a funnel shape at the ends.
Increased size of the vertebral pedicle.

comments: The vertebral pedicles are the two short, thick processes, which connect the body of the spinal vertebra to the arch.

definition.val: A progressive form of decreased height of the intervertebral disk.
Presence of abnormal convexity of the upper and lower end plates of the vertebrae, i.e., an exaggerated bulging out of the upper and lower vertebral end plates.

comments: Note that biconvex vertebral bodies can be a normal finding in newborns.

definition.val: Reduced size of cervical vertebrae.
Anterior tongue-like protrusions of thoracic vertebral bodies.

nodes.lbl: Decreased cervical spine flexion due to contractures of posterior cervical muscles

synonyms.val: Inability to touch chin to chest

definition.val: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation of cervical vertebrae during development.
Over curvature of the lower thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.
Fusion of the C5 and C6 cervical vertebrae.
An elevation of alpha-feto protein measured in the amniotic fluid.

comments: This feature can be found in pregnancies with fetuses affected by a range of abnormalities including for instance encephalocele.

synonyms.val: Elevated amniotic fluid alpha fetal protein

definition.val: Underdevelopment of the nasal bone.
Underdevelopment of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).
Reduced strength of the frontalis muscle (which is located on the forehead).
Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, occurring in the midline region of the face.
A reduced degree of voluntary and involuntary facial movements involved in responded to others or expressing emotions.
Narrow, paramedian longitudinal depressions in the plantar skin of the forefoot.
Outward turning of the heel, resulting in clubfoot with the person walking on the inner part of the foot.

comments: The phrase talipes valgus is derived from the Latin words talus (ankle), pes (poot), and valgus (outward angulation of the distal segment of a bone).

definition.val: Underdevelopment of the Third metatarsal bone leading to a short (hypoplastic) third metatarsal bone.
Short fourth metatarsal bone.
An abnormal thickening of the Achilles tendon.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes two and three.

synonyms.val: Syndactyly of second and third toes

definition.val: Syndactyly with fusion of toes four and five.
The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the calcaneus.
Decrease in mass and density of the metatarsal bones.
Short (hypoplastic) fifth metatarsal bone.

synonyms.val: Hypoplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

definition.val: An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal orientation of the kidney.

comments: The final kidney position in the renal fossa results from the rotation of the kidney with an orientation of the renal pelvis to the medial and the renal calyces to the lateral. Malrotation of the kidney can lead to orientation of the renal pelvis anteriorly, posteriorly and laterally. In most cases, renal malrotation does not cause any symptoms, but, hydronephrosis or stone formation can be observed as complications of renal malformation.

definition.val: Acute renal failure with resolution of manifestations.
An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal axial orientation of the kidney.
An increase in amplitude of waves returned in ultrasonography of the kidney, which is generally displayed as increased brightness of the signal.

synonyms.val: Increased echogenicity of the renal parenchyma

nodes.lbl: Thickening of the glomerular basement membrane

definition.val: Increase in thickness of the basal lamina of the glomerulus of the kidney.

comments: This finding is demonstrated on renal biopsy.

definition.val: The presence of calcium-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

comments: The overwhelming majority of renal calculi contain calcium.

definition.val: A defect in the ability to concentrate the urine.

comments: An impairment in renal concentrating ability can be easily recognized by the maximum concentrating ability (Umax) as determined by the urine osmolality reached after a fixed period of dehydration. Inability to maximally concentrate the urine is related to one or both of two basic tubular defects: 1) a failure of maximal free-water generation by the diluting segment in the ascending limb of Henle's loop; and 2) a failure of the distal tubular epithelium to achieve maximum permeability to water during water deprivation.

definition.val: Acute inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.
A reduction in the ability of the kidneys to remove uric acid from the serum.
Cysts of microscopic size confined to the cortex of the kidney.

A developmental anomaly in which the kidneys are fused and localized on the same side of the midline. This anomaly is thought to result from disruption of the normal embryologic migration of the kidneys.
Complete and diffuse scarring of glomerulus.

comments: All portions of all glomeruli are affected.

definition.val: An abnormality of the renal collecting system.

synonyms.val: Abnormality of the renal collecting system

definition.val: Chronic inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.
Electron dense deposits at the glomerular basement membrane,

comments: Subendothelial electron-dense deposits are a characteristc feature of dense-deposit disease.

definition.val: A type of atrial arrhythmia characterized by atrial rates of between 240 and 400 beats per minute and some degree of atrioventricular node conduction block. Typically, the ventricular rate is half the atrial rate. In the EKG; atrial flutter waves are observed as sawtooth-like atrial activity. Pathophysiologically, atrial flutter is a form of atrial reentry in which there is a premature electrical impulse creates a self-propagating circuit.

comments: Atrial flutter can lead to palpitations, fatigue, dyspnea, and chest pain. Atrial flutter can be paroxysmal or persistent.

definition.val: Episodes of ventricular tachycardia that have a sudden onset and ending.
A form of atrioventricular (AV) dissociation (i.e., the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers) with congenital onset.
AF that cannot be successfully terminated by cardioversion, and longstanding (more than 1 year) AF, where cardioversion is not indicated or has not been attempted, is termed permanent.

comments: The natural history of atrial fibrillation (AF) is characterized by a gradual worsening with time. AF itself produces changes in atrial function and structure. Note there is no precise definition of the duration of AF required to be regarded as chronic.

definition.val: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is an abnormally increased heart rate (over 100 beats per minute at rest) with origin above the level of the ventricles.

comments: A narrow complex (QRS width less than 120 milliseconds) reflects rapid activation of the ventricles via the normal conduction pathway, i.e. His-Purkinje system, which in turn suggests that the tachycardia originated above the AV node and is thus supraventricular.

definition.val: A tachycardia originating in the ventricles characterized by rapid heart rate (over 100 beats per minute) and broad QRS complexes (over 120 ms).

comments: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia that presents as a wide QRS complex tachycardia, and is defined as three or more consecutive QRS complexes with a duration longer than 120 milliseconds (ms) and a rate of 100 beats per minute or more, whereby the complexes have a ventricular origin. VT can be subdivided as follows: (i) sustained VT persists for 30 seconds or more; (ii) non-sustained VT lasts less than 30 seconds; (iii) monomorphic VT displays a uniform QRS morphology; and (iv) polymorphic VT displays QRS morphologies that variy from beat to beat. VT is observed most commonly in individuals with structural heart disease or acute myocardial infarction (MI). VT may also be observed in in the setting of drug toxicity or electrolyte abnormalities or in individuals with Mendelian disease.

definition.val: Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.
Polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias of varying morphologythat do not exist under resting conditions but appear only upon physical exercise or catecholamine administration.

nodes.lbl: obsolete Nodular calcific aortic valve disease

definition.val: Underdevelopment or reduced size of the heart right ventricle, often due to a reduced number of cells.
An episodic form of supraventricular tachycardia with abrupt onset and termination.

comments: PSVT is a term used to denote intermittent supraventricular tachycardia other than atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter and multifocal atrial tachycardia (AT). The major causes are atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT), atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), and sinoatrial node reentrant tachycardia (SNRT).

definition.val: Myxomatous mitral valve is defined as the presence of excess leaflet tissue and leaflet thickening greater than 5 mm, resulting in a prolapse greater than 2 mm into the left atrium on parasternal long axis view.
Decreased number of head hairs per unit area on the anterior region of the scalp.

synonyms.val: Sparse scalp hair at front of head
Thin scalp hair at front of head

definition.val: Fragile, easily breakable scalp hair.
Excessive, increased hair growth located in the elbow region.
Reduced or lacking hair growth of the scalp.

synonyms.val: Reduction in the number of scalp follicle

definition.val: Presence of multiple polyps in the duodenum.

The presence of multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine. The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands. Juvenile polyps are a specific type of hamartomatous polyps.
An anatomical anomaly that results from an abnormal rotation of the gut as it returns to the abdominal cavity during embryogenesis.
Acute hepatitis complicated by acute liver failure with hepatic encephalopathy occurring less than 8 weeks after the onset of jaundice.

comments: Note that different definitions of fulminant hepatitis are used in the medical literature.

definition.val: Fluid retention and edema in the intestine caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
An inability to digest lactose.
Underdevelopment of the small intestine.
Defect in the epithelium of the esophagus, essentially an open sore in the lining of the esophagus.
The presence of a fistula between the perineum and the rectum.
A deviation from the normal rotation of the midgut during embryologic development with mislocalization of the small bowel.

comments: Malrotation results not only in the malposition of the bowel but also in the malfixation of the mesentery. The normally broad mesenteric attachment is shortened to a narrow pedicle that predisposes the patient to the complication of midgut volvulus.

definition.val: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas located in the stomach.
The presence of multiple areas of atresia affecting the small intestine.

nodes.lbl: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract

definition.val: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract.

synonyms.val: Recurrent infection of the GI tract
Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract

definition.val: A form of hemolytic anemia that occurs in repeated episodes.
A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.
A form of leukemia characterized by overproduction of an early myeloid cell.
Low platelet count associated with maternal platelet-specific alloantibodies.

comments: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia occurs following fetomaternal transfusions leading to generation of alloreactive antiplatelet antibodies.

definition.val: A type of hypoplastic anemia with congenital onset.

comments: In this condition, hematopoiesis must have been inadequate in fetal life. Affected infant have marked pallor and reticulocytopenia or absence of red blood cell precursors in an otherwise normally cellular bone marrow. This term does not refer to a particular diagnosis or etiology (or which several are known) but to the phenotypic feature.

definition.val: A type of ALL characterized by elevated levels of B-cell lymphoblasts in the bone marrow and the blood.

Sudden onset of thrombocytopenia (reduced platelet count) within 5-10 days of the transfusion of blood products. The clinical presentation is post-transfusion purpura (PTP), wigth severe thrmbocytopenia, epistaxis, and hemorrhages.

comments: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia is thought to be related to platelet-specific alloantibody from prior transfusion/pregnancy.

definition.val: A kind of hemolytic anemia that is induced by the ingestion of fava beans.

comments: Persons with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency are susceptible to fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia because of the oxidative stress induced by compunds in Fava beans (thought to be vicine and isouramil). The same underlying defect can make affected persons susceptible to hemolysis induced by a number of mediciations.

synonyms.val: Hemolytic anemia following ingestion of fava beans

definition.val: A form of hemolytic anemia that is triggered by ingestion of certain drugs.
A type of hypoplastic anemia in which the erythrocytes have a normal cell volume (the mean corpuscular volume is within normal limits).
An acute leukemia characterized by the proliferation of both neutrophil and monocyte precursors.
An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil.

comments: Neutrophils usually display 3-4 nuclear lobes. Hypersegmented neutrophile nuclei display 5 or more lobes. This feature can be seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency or with other etiologies.

synonyms.val: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

definition.val: A type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence in the blood of erythrocytes of varying sizes and abnormal shapes.
An abnormal increase in the binding affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

A type of megaloblastic anemia that does not improve upon administration of folate. Since vitamin B12 acts by promoting recycling of folate, administration of vitamin B12 also does not improve this type of anemia.

A type of myelodysplastic syndrome characterized by less than 5% myeloblasts in the bone marrow, but with 15% or greater red cell precursors in the marrow being abnormal iron-stuffed cells called ringed sideroblasts.
Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.
A type of acute myeloid leukemia in which abnormal promyelocytes predominate.
A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.
A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.
A type of hemolytic anemia in which the Coombs test is positive.

comments: The Coombs test measures a coating of immunoglobulin or complement on the red cell surface.

definition.val: The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.
Bleeding that persists longer than the normal time following a surgical procedure.

A subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that results from a reciprocal translocation between the ABL-1 oncogene and a breakpoint cluster region (BCR), resulting in a fusion gene, BCR-ABL, that encodes an oncogenic protein with constitutively active tyrosine kinase activity.
Repeated episodes of the formation of a blot clot in a deep vein.
A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of folate.
A decreased alkaline phosphatase activity measured within leukocytes.
Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.
An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.

comments: Protein S functions as a cofactor to Protein C in the inactivation of Factors Va and VIIIa in the coagulation pathway. Therefore, a defect in protein S is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

definition.val: A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.
A type of anemia characterized by abnormally large erythrocytes with abnormally high amounts of haemoglobin.
Thrombocytopenia related to lack of or severe reduction in the count of megakaryocytes.
A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.
A type of sideroblastic anemia that is not responsive to treatment.
Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.
An chronic form of hemolytic anemia.
The presence of a fistula between the bowel and the perineum.

comments: The perineum is the diamond-shaped region of the body between the pubic arch and the anus.

definition.val: An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.
Pneumothorax occurring neonatally without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.
Lack of strength of the intercostal muscles, i.e., of the muscle groups running along the ribs that create and move the chest wall.
Episodic hyperventilation.
Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections in early life, as manifested by recurrent episodes of respiratory infections.
A state of respiratory distress that requires a life saving intervention in the form of gaining airway access and instituting positive pressure ventilation.

nodes.lbl: Intermittent episodes of respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

definition.val: An abnormally elevated blood pressure in the circulation of the pulmonary artery.
Increased susceptibility to infections due to aspiration, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infections due to aspiration.
A form of lactic acidemia that occurs in relation to stress or infection.
A continuous form of lactic acidemia.
A severe form of lactic acidemia.
A form of lactic acidemia that occurs following exercise or exertion.
A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

The term Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) was initially used for patients diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia that could be treated without insulin for more than two years, where the initial diagnosis was made at a young age (under 25 years). Thus, MODY combines characteristics of type 1 diabetes (young age at diagnosis) and type 2 diabetes (less insulin dependence than type 1 diabetes). The term MODY is now most often used to refer to a group of monogenic diseases with these characteristics. Here, the term is used to describe hyperglycemia diagnosed at a young age with no or minor insulin dependency, no evidence of insulin resistence, and lack of evidence of autoimmune destruction of the beta cells.

synonyms.val: Maturity onset diabetes of the young

definition.val: A reduced concentration of vitamin A.
Repeated transient episodes of metabolic acidosis, that is, of the buildup of acid or depletion of base due to accumulation of metabolic acids.
An intermittent (discontinuous) form of lactic acidemia.
Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood occurring during the infantile period.

synonyms.val: Recurrent low blood sugar in infant

definition.val: An impairment of galactose metabolism.
An abnormality of magnesium ion homeostasis.
An increased concentration of L-phenylalanine in the blood.
An abnormal resistance to glucose, i.e., a reduction in the ability to maintain glucose levels in the blood stream within normal limits following oral administration of glucose.
A chronic form of lactic acidemia.

nodes.lbl: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction

definition.val: An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.

synonyms.val: Abnormality of the lung blood vessels

definition.val: Arteriosclerosis (increased thickness, increased stiffness, loss of elasticity) of the small arteries of the brain.

synonyms.val: Hardened artery wall in small cerebral arteries

definition.val: A separation of the layers within the wall of the ascending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.

comments: According to the Stanford classification, type A aortic dissection affects the ascending aorta and arch.

definition.val: Abnormal calcification of the vasculature.
A congenital anomaly with a narrowing or complete absence of the opening between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.

comments: Pulmonary artery atresia means that unoxygenated blood in the right ventricle can not be effectively pumped into the lung for oxygenation.

An aneurysm (severe localized balloon-like outward bulging) in the pulmonary artery.
Excessive bending, twisting, and winding of a cerebral artery.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts, affecting arteries distributed throughout the body.
Increased pressure in the pre-hepatic portal vein.

comments:
Hypertension in the portal venous tree proper.

definition.val: Aortic dilatation refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted (ratio of observed to expected diameter 1.5 or more). Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.

comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe (pathological) form of dilatation of a segment of a blood vessel. In clinical practice, dilatation and aneurysm are occasionally used interchangably. In this subhierarchy, we therefore use aneurysm as the primary label and list dilatation as a broad synonym.

synonyms.val: Bulge in wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

definition.val: Atherosclerosis which occurs in a person with certain risk factors (e.g., SLE, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of early heart disease) at an earlier age than would occur in another person without those risk factors.
The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.

comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

definition.val: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.
An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.
Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.

comments: The ankle-brachial index (ABI; the ratio of systolic blood pressure in the ankle to that in the arm), is a measure of occlusion of peripheral arteries in the leg. Peripheral arterial stenosis may be observed with atherosclerosis and with increased intima media thickness as seen in diseases such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The most common cause of peripheral arterial stenosis in patients over 40 years of age is atherosclerosis. Cerebral and coronary arteries are by definition not included in peripheral artery disease.

definition.val: A rare vascular anomaly with a direct communication between pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed.

nodes.lbl: obsolete Dilatation of the descending aorta

definition.val: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.
An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta.

synonyms.val: Dilatation of the descending thoracic aorta

definition.val: A congenital defect with aplasia (absence) of one of the right or left pulmonary artery.

comments: This is a rare feature that has been observed in recessive lethal osteogenesis imperfecta with mutation in CRTAP.

definition.val: An anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery, such that it arises from the posterior aspect of the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and esophagus to reach the left hilum.
An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the thoracic aorta.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.

comments: Note that the phrase "aortic calcification" is mainly used to describe calcification of the aortic valve rather than of the aorta itself.

definition.val: Increase in mass of the tunica media of the arteries in the pulmonary circulation.

synonyms.val: Hypertrophy of the pulmonary artery wall

definition.val: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large (conduit) arteries.
Recurrent bleeding into the parenchyma of the brain.
Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.
An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.

comments: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

synonyms.val: Aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
Bulging of wall of large artery located above heart

definition.val: Underdevelopment of the pulmonary artery.
An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.
Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the abdominal aorta.

Abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.

definition.val: Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.
Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).

Absent/underdeveloped end part of innermost thighbone

definition.val: An abnormally flat form of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

definition.val: Congenital onset bending or abnormal curvature of the femur that normalizes with age.

comments: This feature can be diagnosed based on the medical history of congenital femoral bowing with spontaneous improvement.

definition.val: The humerus is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.

synonyms.val: Dumbbell-shaped long bone in upper arm

definition.val: Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
Abnormally developed (dysplastic) distal epiphysis of the radius.

Wide innermost wide portion of shinbone bone

Underdevelopment of the ulna on only one side.
An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the proximal portions of the radius and the ulna.
Multiple exostoses originating in long bones.

synonyms.val: Multiple exostoses of long tubular bones

definition.val: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth capital femoral epiphysis.

synonyms.val: Irregular end part of innermost thighbone

definition.val: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the proximal end of the humerus (at the shoulder).
An elevation in bone density of the cortex of one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterolateral direction.
Bony outgrowths that extend laterally from the margin of the metaphysis.

synonyms.val: Fragmented, irregular end part of bone

synonyms.val: Overgrowth of innermost part of calf bone

The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.
A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterior direction.
A limited ability of the knee joint extension and flexion.
An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.
A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.
The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.

synonyms.val: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

definition.val: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.
A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

nodes.lbl: Premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes

synonyms.val: Premature birth following premature rupture of foetal membranes

definition.val: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).

comments: High frequency hearing impairment often involves loss of ability to hear consonants such as s, f, t, and z, even though vowels can be heard normally.

definition.val: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.
Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.
Underdevelopment of the nasal septum.

synonyms.val: Decreased size of septum of nose

comments: This is a category for overall abnormal morphology that may be replaced later with more exact descriptions.

definition.val: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral discs.
An abnormality of the sacral bone.

comments: The sacrum is the large, roughly triangular bone at the base of the verterbal column that is formed by fusion of the five sacral vertebrae S1 to S5.

definition.val: An abnormality of the intervertebral disk.

comments: Any abnormality of the fibrocartilaginous structures that are located between adjacent vertebral bodies.

definition.val: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.

comments: The ventricular response to atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular because of the large number of atrial impulses that transit the atrioventricular node, making the ventricle partially refractory to further impulses. Atrial fibrillation can cause a number of manifestations including excessive ventricular response with angina pectoris or hypotension in susceptible individuals, syncope, systemic embolization, fatigue, or anxiety. These features should be coded separately.

synonyms.val: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

nodes.lbl: obsolete Dilatation of the ascending aorta

definition.val: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.
An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

nodes.lbl: obsolete Abnormalities of the peripheral arteries

definition.val: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.

comments: Supraventricular arrhythmia includes atrial arrhythmias (atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, junctional ectopic tachycardia, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (Wolf-Parkinson-White Syndrome), orthodromic or antidromic. Supraventricular arrhythmia is distinct from ventricular tachycardia, which originates in the ventricles.

definition.val: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.
Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.

comments: Normal diastolic blood pressure is less than 80 mmHg.

definition.val: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.
An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.

comments: The posterior vertebral scalloping sign appears on a lateral radiograph of the spine as an exaggeration of the normal concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies. Neurofibromatosis may be associated with marked scalloping of the posterior borders of the vertebral bodies resulting from intraspinal tumors.

definition.val: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.
Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle.
Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.

comments: The distinctive feature of APVS is the airway obstruction caused by tracheobronchial compression that results from massive dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (PA) and its first- and second-order branches. Consequential tracheomalacia and bronchomalacia determine the timing and severity of respiratory compromise, as well as the morbidity and mortality of these patients.

definition.val: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.
Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.

comments: MAC is a common degenerative process involving the fibrous annulus of the mitral valve, and is generally an incidental finding associated with aging. This term applies if MAC occurs at a substantially younger age than usual.

nodes.lbl: Anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta

definition.val: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.
The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.
Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.
Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.
Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.
An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.
Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.

comments: Blood flow to the aorta distal to the coarctation may be dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus, and hence closure of the ductus arteriosus can lead to serious ischemia of the affected tissues.

definition.val: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.

comments: This HPO term intends to refer to the histological changes that characterize histiocytoid cardiomyopthy. The disease entity Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by incessant ventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, and often sudden death by age 2 years.

definition.val: A ventircular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).
Underdeveloped, small left heart atrium
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.

comments: Pulmonary veins drain through abnormal connections to the right atrium.

definition.val: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.
A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.
Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.
An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.

comments: Elevated mean right atrial pressure (RAP) can be measured by cardiac catheterization.

nodes.lbl: Complete heart block with broad QRS complexes

definition.val: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.
Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.
Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.

comments: An important feature in the differential diagnosis between valvular and subvalvular aortic stenosis is the fact that no ejection sound is present in the latter.

definition.val: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.
Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

nodes.lbl: Complete heart block with narrow QRS complexes

definition.val: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.
Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.

comments: This term should not be applied to Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve (see HP:0010316).

definition.val: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.
The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.

comments: The pulmonary valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid.

definition.val: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.
Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.

comments: The metatarsal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the toes.

synonyms.val: Flattened head of long bone of foot

definition.val: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.
Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

nodes.lbl: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature

definition.val: Absence of the abdominal musculature.
A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.

comments: The bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori has co-evolved with humans and colonizes approximately half of the human population, but only causes overt gastric disease in a subset of infected hosts.

definition.val: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.

comments: Esophageal perforation can lead to retained gastric contents, saliva, bile, and other substances entering the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinitis, which in turn may lead to sepsis.

definition.val: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.
Hypertrophy of the stomach.
Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.
The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.
Underdevelopment of the colon.

Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.
The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.
Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.
Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.
An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.

comments: Chewing and swallowing are interrelated. The act of chewing plays a fundamental role in the process of swallowing food. Mastication prepares food for swallowing by breaking it into small particles. Accordingly, loss of teeth has been associated with swallowing difficulties. Chewing difficulties may be caused by loss of teeth, partial dentures, or by tooth pain. Swallowing difficulties, in contrast, are often characterized by difficulties swallowing liquids, reflux, throat spasms, choking on dry food, or dysphagia.

definition.val: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.
Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.

comments: This feature can be ascertained by immunoassay of gastric juices.

synonyms.val: Intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

definition.val: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.
A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.
Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.

comments: This finding can be observed upon abdominal radiography. The bowel lumen may be slightly dilated. Secondary to the fluid accumulation, there are anatomic and motor alterations in the intestine which are reflected in the roentgenogram.

definition.val: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.
Obstruction affecting the biliary tree.
A chronic form of gastritis.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.

comments: Dysplasia is defined in MPATH as a distortion or deficiency of the tissue or cellular architecture.

definition.val: The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.
A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.
A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.
The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.
A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.
Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.
Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

synonyms.val: Death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

definition.val: Developmental hypoplasia of the intestine.
A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

nodes.lbl: Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature

definition.val: Underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.
Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.
Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor.

nodes.lbl: Unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle

definition.val: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.

synonyms.val: Unilateral aplasia of pectoralis major muscle

nodes.lbl: Abnormal facility in opposing the shoulders

definition.val: Hemorrhage occurring within a joint.
The presence of inflammation of the gastric mucous membrane.
An abnormality of the gallbladder.
An abnormality of the jejunum, i.e., of the middle section of the small intestine.
A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

nodes.lbl: Premature delivery because of cervical insufficiency or membrane fragility

definition.val: A pregnancy that ends at a stage in which the fetus is incapable of surviving on its own, defined as the spontaneous loss of a fetus before the 20th week of pregnancy.

Exaggerated bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion, or commissure).
Lack of the cartilage of the nasal septum.

synonyms.val: Failure of development of nasal septal cartilage
Decreased size of tip of nose

definition.val: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.

comments: The adjective "depressed" here does not indicate an active process but a status. A depressed nasal bridge can occur irrespective of the width of the nasal bridge, and the width should be assessed independently. In infancy, the nasal bridge is relatively more posterior than in the older person. The term depressed nasal bridge should only be used when the bridge is more posterior than is typical for age and ethnic background.

synonyms.val: Decreased size of bridge of nose

definition.val: Abnormality of the nostril.

synonyms.val: Decreased size of internal carotid artery
